rationale: A defensible extension that adds maturing principal to the validated interest-plus-dividend burden and recasts it in the bounded share form, though it is largely an amalgam of two existing archive winners (CommittedCashBurdenPerProfit and CapitalMarketDependenceIndex) and risks capturing the same distress/leverage variation rather than new information.

This is the textbook dividend payout ratio, one of the most heavily studied accounting ratios in the literature (Lintner, Arnott–Asness, payout-vs-growth work), and as a single-component decomposition of an existing archive signal it is too trivial and too well-known to count as a novel cross-theme test.

(oibdp − xint − dvt)/at is essentially the canonical Fama–French/Ball et al. operating profitability measure (which itself subtracts interest expense) with a small dividend adjustment, so it rediscovers the profitability anomaly and will be substantially absorbed by RMW in the very FF5 alpha used to evaluate it.

A well-diagnosed, economically substantive repair rather than a cosmetic variant — rescaling net repayment by the lagged debt stock it actually reduces fixes the identified denominator pathology (tiny-oancf firms populating the top decile) that plausibly explains the strong slope with null alpha, though the structural resemblance to ProfitableSelfFundedDeleveraging means the result must be judged against that baseline.

The expression's direction is internally consistent with the negative expected sign and the conditioner is motivated by the specific slope/alpha divergence in CommittedCashBurdenPerProfit, but one-year margin deltas have repeatedly been the weak leg in this archive and the weakest-link MIN may simply thin the encumbered tail rather than sharpen it.

Sign and construction are coherent and it fills a genuine gap (a wide-coverage long-side candidate), but the low-encumbrance leg mechanically selects high-profit non-dividend-payers with little interest expense, so the signal risks being a repackaged profitability-plus-low-leverage composite that FF5's RMW and CMA already span.
